posts.title: Getting started with Express middleware
posts.content: Middleware functions run before your route handlers and can inspect, modify, or reject a request. Auth checks, logging, and body parsing are all classic use cases.

posts.title: Why we switched from Mongoose to Sequelize
posts.content: MongoDB is great for flexible schemas, but once we needed real foreign keys between users, posts, and categories, a relational database made the relationships much easier to enforce.

posts.title: Understanding JWTs in 5 minutes
posts.content: A JSON Web Token is a signed, not encrypted, blob of data. Anyone can read the payload, but only your server can verify it was actually issued by you.

posts.title: Controlled inputs in React, explained
posts.content: A controlled input ties its displayed value directly to React state, so the UI and your data can never drift out of sync — every keystroke updates state, which re-renders the input.

posts.title: Why we built a custom axios wrapper
posts.content: Instead of repeating auth headers on every request, one preconfigured axios instance with interceptors handles attaching the token and catching 401s in a single place.

posts.title: Zero-downtime deploys with GitHub Actions
posts.content: Running migrations and restarting the server in the wrong order is the most common way to take a site down during a deploy. Here's the sequencing we settled on.
